elements.text: You have gallstones which are causing attacks of pain.
We remove your gallbladder through 3-4 small cuts using a camera; we fill your tummy with gas to see.
No more attacks; prevents complications (inflammation, jaundice, pancreatitis).

Wound infection (roughly 1-5%); bleeding; bile leak (about 0.5%, pooled 0.46%); major injury to the main bile duct (about 0.3%, pooled 0.28%, may need major repair); stone left in duct; conversion to open (about 2-5% planned operations, up to about 20% in emergency or inflamed cases); shoulder-tip pain from the gas; hernia at cut; ongoing symptoms; clots; bowel injury (rare); death (very rare, under about 0.1%).
Watch and wait, low-fat diet (attacks often return; complications possible).
More attacks, possible inflammation, jaundice, pancreatitis.
Ask what matters most to the patient and answer questions honestly.
We remove your appendix through 3 small cuts, or sometimes one larger cut.
Removes the infection; prevents bursting, abscess and sepsis.

Wound infection (more in open or burst cases); pus collection inside (about 2-5% simple, more if burst); bleeding; injury to bowel or bladder (rare); conversion to open; appendix turns out normal; bowel slow to restart; clots.

For simple appendicitis without a stone inside: antibiotics only. 29% needed appendectomy by 90 days (25% without and 41% with an appendicolith) in the CODA trial (NEJM 2020); 39.1% had recurrence within 5 years in the APPAC trial (JAMA 2018).
Bursting, abscess, peritonitis, sepsis, possibly death.
Ask what matters most to the patient and answer questions honestly.
